# Author and date

The parenthetical mark names the source and its year [@one], and the same key
cited in the collapsed form [@two][] reaches the same entry.

A citation may read in the sentence. As [+@two] showed, the method holds, and
the year alone follows a name the prose already carries: Postigo argued this
in [-@one].

Two sources share one parenthesis when their keys share one bracket with a
semicolon between them [@three; @one], and a source with four authors is
shortened by the style, as [+@four] found.
